title: KV quantization profile synthesis and calibration runbook
creator: Marcus Li
description:
Purpose: Produce a defensible, operationalized pipeline for synthesizing compact KV cache quantization profiles (INT8 and FP8 variants), run calibration across representative workloads, validate accuracy regressions, and codify rollback/rollout policies. This ticket bundles experiment design, tooling changes to the calibration harness, validation criteria, and a playbook for staged rollouts into Dedicated/Hosted backends.

Why now: Prior work produced many per-workload calibration probes but lacked a repeatable synthesis step that merges cross-workload profiles and per-head outlier handling. This causes noisy rollouts and unexpected quality regressions for long-context generation. The goal is to reduce drama by producing a small set (<=3) of vetted profiles that balance latency and quality across typical Redwood workloads.

Scope: 
- Implement a profile-synthesis step that aggregates calibration stats from multiple workloads to produce compact per-layer scaling and optional per-head masks.
- Extend the existing calibration harness to support multi-model runs in parallel, store intermediate histograms, and export reproducible calibration artifacts.
- Run a matrix of FP8 and symmetric/asymmetric INT8 profiles across three canonical workloads (chat-long, code-complete, instruction-complete) with KV enabled.
- Validate with both offline evals and shadow traffic in a pinned Dedicated pool.
- Produce a rollout/runbook with acceptance criteria, fallback trigger thresholds, and monitoring queries.

Non-goals: changing core runtime kernels, model retraining, or deploying global default profiles to Hosted without per-customer shadow validation.
experiment_plan:
Hypothesis: A synthesis approach that 1) identifies per-layer scale factors using pooled activation histograms, 2) masks per-head outliers above 4 sigma, and 3) applies a small bias-correction table will achieve comparable quality to FP32 while reducing KV memory bandwidth and token compute latency by at least 12-18% on A100 and H100-class GPUs.

Matrix: 
- Models: redwood-v1-small (test harness), open-llm-7b, open-llm-30b (quant-friendly variants).
- Profiles: FP8-e4m3, FP8-e4m3-with-bias-corr, INT8-symmetric, INT8-asymmetric, hybrid (INT8 most layers + FP8 on top4).
- Workloads: chat-long (512 KV length), code-complete (1024 KV length), instruction-complete (256 KV length with many short-turns).
- Repetitions: 5 independent calibration seeds per workload/profile.
- Platforms: A100-80GB (nvlink disabled) and H100-80GB (released staging fleet).
datasets: Evaluation sets: redwood/kv-calib-v2 (5000 long-context generative prompts), redwood/evals/llm-regression-suite (QA + code generation subset ~2k samples), top-queries-shadow-2026-02 (anonymized customer-like traces). Calibration inputs: synthetic sequences derived from dataset histograms to exercise extreme KV magnitudes.
metrics: Primary: token-level perplexity delta vs FP32, response-level exact-match (QA), top-5 token divergence rate, mean token latency (p50/p95), KV memory bandwidth per request. Secondary: allocation failure rate, increased retry/fallback rate in shadow. Quality acceptance thresholds defined below.
calibration_steps:
1) Collect activation histograms during standard FP32 runs with KV enabled across workloads.
2) Pool histograms and compute per-layer scaling candidates using a trimmed-mean approach to reduce influence of burst outliers.
3) Detect heavy-tailed heads and generate binary masks for per-head fallback to higher-precision in profiles.
4) For INT8, evaluate symmetric and asymmetric foldings; compute zero-point where beneficial and track quantization error distributions.
5) Optionally run a small bias-correction table optimization (2-10% extra storage) to reduce mean logit shift.
6) Produce reproducible profile artifact (profile id, metadata, checksum, histogram seeds) and run validation suite.
7) Persist artifacts to s3://redwood-quant/profiles/2026-02-14/ with signed metadata and CI gating.
rollout_plan:
Stage 0 - Local CI: gating via unit/integration tests and the regen-suite.
Stage 1 - CI-staging: run full calibration matrix nightly; artifacts must pass acceptance criteria.
Stage 2 - Shadow traffic in Dedicated pool: route 1% shadow traffic for a subset of tenants using a pinned model variant with logging enabled (7 days).
Stage 3 - Canary: 5% live traffic for low-impact customers with automatic rollback if token-level divergence >1.5% or p95 latency increases >20%.
Stage 4 - Gradual ramp to 100% per-region with per-customer opt-out. All rollouts require annotated runbook and an approved PR to runtime-configs.
acceptance_criteria: Quality: token-level perplexity delta <= +0.6% relative to FP32 across the evaluation set OR response-level exact-match drop <= 0.5% on QA subset. Latency: mean token latency improvement >= 12% on A100 or no more than 8% regression on worst-case platform. Operational: no increase in allocation failures or retries above historical baseline by >0.2%. Shadow stability: less than 1% of sessions flagged for manual review.
risks_mitigation:
- Risk: per-head outliers cause rare but high-impact hallucinations. Mitigation: per-head mask with conservative thresholds and telemetry on flagged tokens.
- Risk: bias-correction table shifts scoring distribution on specific benchmarks. Mitigation: run targeted stat tests and keep bias-correction optional per-profile.
- Risk: calibration drift across workloads. Mitigation: schedule weekly re-calibration for high-volume tenants and add drift monitors that compute KL divergence against baseline histograms.
results_summary: (Draft) Preliminary microbench on redwood-v1-small: hybrid profile (INT8 all layers except top 4 FP8) reduced p50 token latency by 16% and p95 by 12% on A100. Token perplexity change was +0.35% and top-5 divergence 0.8% on the calibration set. FP8-only profiles achieved slightly better quality (+0.2% perplexity) but with lower latency gains (9-11%). Per-head masking reduced worst-case divergence from 3.9% to 0.9% on synthetic outlier tests. Full matrix runs on open-llm-30b are queued (scheduled 2026-02-25).
